topic: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)
usual_baseline: The Oakland score is almost never documented: 0–10% in most units, 36% at best. Shock index is recorded in 0–27%. Many clinicians do not know the score (61.8% unaware in one survey). Only 35% of patients were managed appropriately in one unit.
fix_that_works: Education alone gave large gains. Teaching with a summary sheet and e-calculator link: documentation 10% to 42% [2381]. Posters and a teaching session: 4.8% to 48.8% [2849]. A targeted educational intervention: Oakland score 36% to 79%, shock index 27% to 82%, admission rate 53% to 38% [2864].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Even after teaching, over half of patients still had no documented score in two units [2381] [2849].
consultant_advice: Documentation audits here all show the same thing. More useful is whether the score changed decisions: avoidable admissions, safe discharges and unnecessary CT angiograms. Build the score into the clerking proforma rather than relying on teaching, as gains after teaching reached only 42–49% in two units.
